clue.text: Wine distributors invent fantastic rosé every now and then

indicators.note: something fantastic is wildly imaginative, so the word invent is rearranged
taking a letter only now and then from the word picks its alternate letters

explanation.surface: Wine merchants dream up some extraordinary pink wine, now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintners are wine merchants, the traders who sell and supply wine.

clue.text: Intimate meal with no starter

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A cosy dinner for two that skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' suggests a course of the meal, but it means the first letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings are private and personal, as intimate thoughts are.

clue.text: Drums of paint I'm mixing

indicators.note: mixing paint suits the surface, but here it says the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter says they are mixing colours on the drum kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, the large orchestral drums played by a percussionist.

clue.text: Fish in Eastern European lake

explanation.surface: A fish living in a lake somewhere in eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long snakelike fish found in rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Big transformation of a hen's cage, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given are only one arrangement of the result, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Revamping a chicken coop described as a major transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea change, from Shakespeare's Tempest, is a profound or radical alteration.

clue.text: Lots of artics carrying furniture

indicators.note: the lorries are said to carry the answer, which sits inside the words run together

parts.note: the run of letters holding the answer

explanation.surface: Many articulated lorries transporting furniture loads.
explanation.walkthrough: Artics are articulated lorries, the big trucks in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people, a piece of household furniture.

clue.text: Ready for fight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as in prepared and about to act
second meaning: a brief quarrel or scrap

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready for fight' reads as one phrase about being prepared, but it splits into two separate meanings joined by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief scrap or argument, while being set to do something means being poised and prepared.

clue.text: Football group's trial is the least time-consuming

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, the English football governing body, with its possessive S

explanation.surface: The football authority's experiment turns out to be the quickest.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest option is the quickest, the one taking the least time.

clue.text: Handle covered with last drops of some eggshell paint

indicators.note: the name is wrapped by the outer letters on either side
the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A handle painted with the dregs of an eggshell-finish tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggshell' looks like part of the definition, since it is a paint finish, but it only supplies a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy hard-drying paint, a type of coating used on wood and metal.

clue.text: Where you may see England and Australia declare

definitions.text: Where you may see England and Australia
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: at a Test, a Test match between the cricket nations
second meaning: state formally, bear witness

explanation.walkthrough: 'Declare' is also a cricket term, adding to the Ashes picture, but here it simply means state. Test matches are international cricket games; England v Australia is the Ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to affirm or certify something as true, a formal statement.

clue.text: A Republican linked to each district

explanation.surface: A Republican politician is associated with every constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or zone, much like a district of a town.

clue.text: Companion boarding earlier sailing vessel

indicators.note: going aboard means being put inside the other word

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A shipmate climbed aboard a sailing ship ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a fore-and-aft rigged ship with two or more masts.

clue.text: Green veg and Italian sauces served up without warning

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a snap election or decision is sudden, called without warning

explanation.surface: Green vegetables and Italian sauces dished out unannounced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' fits a meal, but in a down entry it signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar snaps are edible-podded peas, a green vegetable eaten whole.

clue.text: Gizmo requires light cleaning at the back

parts.note: thin and light both describe fabric of little weight

indicators.note: the back of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A gadget that needs a light clean at the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any unnamed object or device, much as a gizmo is a gadget.

clue.text: Teams initially joined forces, that's agreed

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Teams came together, and that was settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that tally correspond, so tallied means matched or corresponded.

clue.text: Books about a certain musical ensemble

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters go round the next piece

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
one as in 'one Mr Smith', a certain person

explanation.surface: Books written on a particular group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, a chamber ensemble.

clue.text: A robin flying over one city

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above the next piece
a bird flying around is in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A robin flies over a single city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: A learner had to acquire vehicle with plenty of options?

indicators.note: acquiring something means holding it, so it goes inside

parts.note: ate as in had a meal

explanation.surface: A learner driver had to get a car with lots of optional extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' means ate, as in had dinner, which links back to the menu sense of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a la carte means choosing from a full menu rather than a set meal.

clue.text: Rate elements of each idea

indicators.note: only some parts of the words, run together, are used

parts.note: the run of letters holding the answer

explanation.surface: Assess the components of every concept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' looks like assess, but here it means berate.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone, in an older sense, is to scold them severely.

clue.text: Revered person picked up for doing nothing

indicators.note: picked up as by a microphone, so it is how the word sounds

explanation.surface: A hero chosen for his laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means inactive or unoccupied, not working at anything.

clue.text: Large signs for golf course

parts.note: inks as in inks a deal, signs it

explanation.surface: Big notices put up around a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Links are seaside golf courses on sandy ground, the classic Scottish type.

clue.text: Underling working next to car

parts.note: the Mini is a classic small British car
on as in switched on, working

explanation.surface: A junior employee at work beside a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a subordinate follower, a lowly servant.

clue.text: Father has puzzled looks

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for a priest's title Father

explanation.surface: Dad gives perplexed glances.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowns are furrowed brows, expressions of confusion or displeasure.

clue.text: Take time away from flipping stupid craze

indicators.note: flipping turns the remaining letters over, read in reverse
the abbreviation for time is removed

explanation.surface: Stop wasting hours on a ridiculous trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word qualifying stupid, but it signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: A fad is a short-lived craze, a passing fashion.

clue.text: Border of grass trimmed at the front

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: sedge is a grasslike plant of wet ground

explanation.surface: A lawn border with its front cut neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a boundary or rim, a margin like a border.

clue.text: New pet dog is fatter than the rest

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly adopted pet dog is the chubbiest of the litter.
explanation.definitionFit: Podgiest is the superlative of podgy, meaning plump or chubby beyond all others.
